newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL blue chips slump as central bank tightens.
newsitem.headline: KL blue chips slump as central bank tightens.

text.p: Malaysian shares slumped on Monday after the central Bank Negara announced proposals to tighten loans for property and share buying and maintain a tight monetary policy, dealers said.
The benchmark Composite Index of 100 large-capitalised stocks lost 14.54 points, or 1.19 percent to 1,203.10. It had dropped as low as 1,194.53 or by 1.9 percent, in the afternoon.
Bank Negara said it was maintaining its tight monetary policy, dashing hopes of an easing in the second half of the year, dealers said.

"Interest rates now look as if they are going to go up. Most economists expected interest rates to go the other way, because they need to maintain short-term inflows of funds," said William Chan, a dealer at Seagroatt & Campbell.

"People were expecting interest rates to ease off in the second half. With the new Bank Negara rulings there's no chance. Some of them are re-rating property and finance stocks," said an institutional dealer at a bank-backed brokerage.
The Kuala Lumpur property index of listed property-related stocks shed 96.42 points or 3.5 percent, finishing at 2,656.52.
